textoCompleto: A young shepherd boy lived in a small village. His job was to watch the sheep on the hill near the forest. Every day, he sat alone while the sheep ate grass. The boy was very bored. One day, he decided to play a trick. He ran down to the village and shouted as loud as he could, 'Wolf! Wolf! A wolf is attacking the sheep!' The villagers heard his cries and ran up the hill to help him. They carried sticks and tools to chase the wolf away. But when they arrived, there was no wolf. The boy laughed and laughed. 'You fools! There is no wolf! I tricked you!' The villagers were angry. 'Do not cry wolf if there is no wolf,' they warned him. A few days later, the boy was bored again. He shouted, 'Wolf! Wolf! Please help me!' The villagers came running again. But again, there was no wolf. The boy laughed once more. The villagers were very angry. 'If you cry wolf again, we will not help you,' they said. The next day, a real wolf came. The wolf was big and hungry. The boy was terrified. He ran down the hill and screamed, 'Wolf! Wolf! Please, help! A real wolf is here!' The villagers heard him, but they thought it was another trick. 'He is lying again,' they said. No one came to help. The wolf ate all the sheep. The boy learned a very important lesson: if you tell lies, people will not believe you even when you tell the truth.
